final.q: The API response includes an extra, undocumented field, and your test passes because the schema allows additional properties. What do you do?
o: Nothing: green is green
I tighten the schema (strict), report the undocumented field with evidence and ask for the contract to be updated
I document the field myself in my test
I add the field to the schema as optional
final.why: An undocumented response is a finding. The strict schema IS the contract test; permissive = false green.

final.q: Cycle 1: 3 tests fail. The fix arrives, you rerun those 3 and they go green. Can you close the test cycle?
o: Yes: what failed now passes
No: the full regression at the end is still missing — the fix may have broken something else
Yes, if the dev confirms the change was small
Only if the PO approves it
final.why: “Iterate narrow, confirm wide”: the narrow retest iterates fast, but you close with a full regression.

final.q: A vendor bug blocks 2 scenarios. The PO asks to close the user story “with the @IGNORE in place”. What do you answer?
o: I close it: that's what the tag is for
@IGNORE excludes them from the run, but the ticket stays Open and the story does NOT close until it's resolved
I close it if the PO puts it in writing
I delete the 2 scenarios and close it
final.why: @IGNORE manages the run, not the commitment: closing the story with an open known issue is masking it on the board.

final.q: Green pipeline, full traceability, and a bot signs off automatically. Is the certification valid?
o: Yes: it meets all the technical requirements
No: the sign-off is a human judgment of risk; the bot can only prepare the evidence package
Yes, if the bot uses the QA lead's account
It depends on the company
final.why: Everything else can be automated; accountability can't. “Certification is signed by a human.”

final.q: The regression suite has been all green for months and the team wants to “take advantage” by trimming it. What does the method say?
o: Trim it: sustained green = confidence
Review it against the pesticide paradox: vary data/scenarios and re-prioritize by risk before touching its size
Freeze it as it is forever
Duplicate it to be safe
final.why: Sustained green can mean immunized tests, not healthy software. First you refresh it, then you decide on size.

final.q: You see this step: When I click on "#submit-btn" and wait 3 seconds. What's the diagnosis?
o: Correct: it's explicit
Imperative Gherkin coupled to the UI: the business intent is lost and the feature breaks with every CSS change
Valid if the selector is stable
It's just missing the Then
final.why: The feature states WHAT happens in the business; selectors and waits live in the steps. Coupling them turns it into pure maintenance.

final.q: You have budget to automate just ONE thing this month. Which do you pick?
o: The checkout flow that 90% of customers use and that changes every sprint
A stable legacy screen nobody touches
The contact form
The landing page styles
final.why: Rate of change × criticality = the highest return on automation. Stable, trivial things don't pay for their maintenance.

final.q: Your TS suite compiles perfectly with correct types. Have you validated the API contract yet?
o: Yes: TypeScript validates the types
No: types are erased at compile time — the contract is validated at runtime with Zod/AJV against the schema
Yes, if I use generics in the HTTP client
Only the 200 status is left
final.why: A generic is a promise to the compiler, not a check on the service. Runtime schema validation, or there's no contract test.

final.q: To “stabilize” the suite, a teammate adds sleep(5000) to 40 tests. What's the real problem?
o: None, if they pass now
It hides the cause (wrong locators/waits), adds 3+ minutes per run and the flakiness will come back with a different latency
That 5 seconds is too short
That they should have used sleep(10000)
final.why: A sleep is debt: it charges interest on every run and the synchronization bug is still alive underneath.

final.q: You need to test the same app with 3 roles (admin, editor, viewer). What's the right way to set it up in Playwright?
o: One giant test that logs in 3 times
storageState per role + projects/fixtures: each test runs authenticated with the role it declares
3 copies of the repo
Swapping the DB between tests
final.why: A persisted session per role, declared as a fixture: readable RBAC, fast, and no repeated logins through the UI.

final.q: p99 spikes ONLY when traffic jumps suddenly (campaigns). Which test reproduces it?
o: A 6-hour soak
Spike: sudden load increases to see whether the system absorbs them and recovers
A smoke test on every deploy
A unit test of the endpoint
final.why: Each type targets a risk: a spike test models exactly the sudden hit that drives up your p99.

final.q: A flaky test lives in the PR quality gate. What's the biggest damage if you leave it there?
o: Slower runs
The team learns to ignore reds and rerun the pipeline: the gate loses all authority
Wasted CI minutes
None, if it passes on the second try
final.why: The day “red” means “just rerun it”, the gate is dead. Immediate quarantine and a root-cause fix.

final.q: In an audit, someone asks about a green from 2 sprints ago and there's no evidence attached. What's the state of the sign-off?
o: Valid: the test passed
Compromised: a green you can't defend invalidates the certification — evidence is part of done
Valid if the QA remembers it well
Valid because CI keeps logs for 7 days
final.why: Certifying = being able to show what was tested, when and with what result. Without evidence, all that's left is your word.

final.q: The AI hands you the suite and the diff includes a schema change so that “the test passes”. What do you do?
o: Merge: the AI knows the context
I reject that part: it's the masking anti-pattern — the schema comes from the contract, not from the response
Merge with a TODO to review later
I ask another AI for a second opinion
final.why: It's THE anti-pattern AI commits with confidence. Your role as director exists precisely to catch this.

final.q: A flawless 5-block prompt, but the AI doesn't know your project. Typical result:
o: Excellent: the prompt is everything
Generic, with made-up assumptions: “context before prompt” — without CLAUDE.md/notes, even the best prompt delivers little
Perfect if you use the newest model
A tool error
final.why: A brilliant prompt on poor context produces plausible code for SOME OTHER project. Context first.

final.q: Which of these decisions can you fully delegate to the AI?
o: Whether the contract mismatch blocks the release
Which risks to prioritize this sprint
Generating the POM boilerplate on top of a clear, existing convention
Signing the story's certification
final.why: Mechanical + clear convention + reversible = delegable. Risk, priority and sign-off are yours.

final.q: You're automating against a shared environment and a key record shows up as “deactivated” (empty 204). What do you do?
o: I report a service bug
I check for the caveat in the dataset documentation; if it's not there, I document it — data with special states is part of the design
I set the record back to active from the DB
I hardcode another ID that works
final.why: “Without data, nothing runs”: a dataset documented with its caveats is a deliverable, not a nuisance.

final.q: You find a critical mismatch 2 days before the release. How do you communicate it to the stakeholder?
o: “My test fails, we can't ship”
Evidence (cURL + response) + impact on the consumer + options with their cost/risk
I mention it at tomorrow's daily
I escalate it to the dev and wash my hands of it
final.why: Detector→impact→options. The stakeholder decides with your evidence; you're not the blocker, you're the radar.

final.q: You're moved from Xray to TestRail and from Allure to another reporter. What survives of your method?
o: Nothing: relearn from scratch
Everything essential: the requirement→case→execution→evidence chain and the sign-off standard are tool-agnostic
Only the Gherkin
Only the API tests
final.why: That's why the method is worth more than the stack: brands rotate, the standard of evidence and traceability doesn't.

final.q: Sprint closed: full suite green, 85% coverage, zero open bugs. What do you tell the team?
o: “The software is fine”
“My tests, as designed, found no problems — and this is what they cover and this is what they don't”
“We can skip next sprint's regression”
“Quality is guaranteed”
final.why: The honest statement sets the scope. Green ≠ guarantee; it's the absence of findings WITHIN what was designed.

final.q: What does a 100 % kill rate on your mutant catalog prove?
o: That the software has no bugs
That your suite caught every mutant in YOUR catalog; mutants you didn't write may survive
That coverage is 100 %
That regression is no longer needed
final.why: The kill rate measures the suite against the mutants that exist. It's evidence about your checks, not a guarantee about the software.

final.q: An AI assistant wrote the tests and also their asserts, and everything is green. What do you do before signing off?
o: I sign off
I mutate the product or the contract on purpose and check that those tests turn red
I ask it for another summary
I add retries
final.why: When code and tests come from the same place, a green proves less than it seems. Test the tester.

final.q: Where do you put a rule that must never be broken in a workflow with AI assistants?
o: In the prompt
In a hook or in CI, with a non-zero exit code and cases that try to get around it
In an Obsidian note
In the chat
final.why: A prompt can be ignored; a hook or a CI gate can't, and on top of that they can be tested.

final.q: Your judge-based evaluation scored 93 % on the same cases you used to tune the threshold. Which number do you report?
o: That 93 %
The one from a held-out set the tuning never saw, with its interval
The best of several runs
The model provider's number
final.why: The honest number is the one the tuning didn't touch.

final.q: Your pipeline comes out green, but the test step ends in || true. What does that green tell you?
o: That the tests passed
Nothing about the tests: that step can't fail
That the lint passed
That there's branch protection
final.why: A gate that can't fail isn't a gate. Testing the tester includes testing the pipeline.

final.q: The ephemeral runner died in the middle of the run. What evidence do you have left?
o: Everything that was on its disk
Only what you uploaded beforehand as an artifact or receipt (logs, hashes, reports)
The full cache
Never anything
final.why: Design it so the evidence gets out before the container dies.
